es: Identificar el punto, la razón, el ejemplo y el cierre en respuestas improvisadas, reconocer tangentes y decidir cuál de varias respuestas está mejor ordenada y por qué.

teaching.en: A well-built answer opens with the point, stated in one sentence: my point is that cities need more bike lanes.
teaching.es: Una respuesta bien construida empieza por el punto, dicho en una frase: mi punto es que las ciudades necesitan más ciclovías.
teaching.explanationEs: El punto es tu postura, dicha en una sola frase y al principio.
segments: A well-built answer opens with the point, stated in one
sentence: my point is that cities need more bike lanes.
teaching.audioText: A well-built answer opens with the point, stated in one sentence: my point is that cities need more bike lanes.

teaching.en: The main reason should follow at once, because an opinion with no reason gives the listener nothing to weigh.
teaching.es: La razón principal debe venir enseguida, porque una opinión sin razón no le da al oyente nada que valorar.
teaching.explanationEs: La razón explica por qué piensas así: The main reason is that…
segments: The main reason should follow at once, because an opinion
with no reason gives the listener nothing to weigh.
teaching.audioText: The main reason should follow at once, because an opinion with no reason gives the listener nothing to weigh.

teaching.en: Then add an example, such as accidents falling in my neighbourhood after the new lane opened, to drive the point home.
teaching.es: Después añade un ejemplo, como que los accidentes bajaron en mi barrio cuando se abrió la nueva ciclovía, para dejar clara la idea.
teaching.explanationEs: El ejemplo apoya la razón con un caso concreto; drive the point home = dejarlo claro.
segments: Then add an example, such as accidents falling in my neighbourhood
after the new lane opened, to drive the point home.
teaching.audioText: Then add an example, such as accidents falling in my neighbourhood after the new lane opened, to drive the point home.

teaching.en: Close with a conclusion that repeats your point in fresh words rather than introducing a brand-new idea.
teaching.es: Cierra con una conclusión que repita tu punto con otras palabras en lugar de introducir una idea nueva.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre devuelve al oyente a tu punto, no abre otro tema.
segments: Close with a conclusion that repeats your point in
fresh words rather than introducing a brand-new idea.
teaching.audioText: Close with a conclusion that repeats your point in fresh words rather than introducing a brand-new idea.

teaching.en: If you go off on a tangent, admit it briefly and get to the point; a rambling answer makes listeners lose the thread.
teaching.es: Si te vas por las ramas, admítelo brevemente y ve al grano; una respuesta que divaga hace que los oyentes pierdan el hilo.
teaching.explanationEs: Reconocer el desvío y volver al punto evita perder el orden.
segments: If you go off on a tangent, admit it briefly and get
to the point; a rambling answer makes listeners lose the thread.
teaching.audioText: If you go off on a tangent, admit it briefly and get to the point; a rambling answer makes listeners lose the thread.

teaching.en: To stay on track, name your point, reason, example and conclusion in your head and check each one as you speak.
teaching.es: Para no desviarte, nombra mentalmente tu punto, razón, ejemplo y conclusión y ve comprobando cada uno mientras hablas.
teaching.explanationEs: Las cuatro etiquetas mentales funcionan como un mapa mientras improvisas.
segments: To stay on track, name your point, reason, example and conclusion
in your head and check each one as you speak.

prompt.es: Une cada frase con la parte de la respuesta que es.

pairs: My view is that a longer break would help.
The main reason is that students get tired.
To illustrate, last week half the class fell asleep.
In conclusion, a longer break is worth it.

feedback.es: Cada arranque marca una parte: my view declara la postura, the main reason explica, to illustrate ilustra e in conclusion cierra.

hint.es: Mira cómo empieza cada frase: postura, razón, ejemplo o cierre.

pairs: My view is that a longer break would help.
The main reason is that students get tired.
To illustrate, last week half the class fell asleep.
In conclusion, a longer break is worth it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Perdón, estoy divagando; voy al grano.»

feedback.es: Get to the point es volver a lo esencial después de un desvío.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que designa la idea central que se defiende.

origin.text: Halfway through her answer, the student noticed that she was drifting away from the topic. “Sorry, I'm rambling; let me get to the ___,” she said.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del texto funciona como ejemplo?

choices.text: The claim that free buses would reduce traffic across the whole town.
The idea that free buses benefit everyone who lives in the town.
The town's month-long trial, after which the roads were quieter.

feedback.es: El ejemplo es el caso concreto de la prueba de un mes; la afirmación sobre el tráfico es la razón y la referencia a todos es el cierre.

hint.es: Un ejemplo cuenta un caso concreto que ocurrió, no una idea general.

origin.text: My point is that buses should be free. The main reason is that they reduce traffic. For instance, my town tried it for a month, and the roads were much quieter. In conclusion, free buses benefit everyone.

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta y elige qué frase funciona como ejemplo.

choices.text: Children returning to play in the closed old town.
The air becoming much cleaner in the city centre.
The centre belonging to people and not to engines.

feedback.es: El ejemplo es el caso concreto de la ciudad que cerró su casco antiguo; el aire limpio es la razón y la frase de los motores es el cierre.

origin.audio: Should cities ban cars from their centres? My point is yes. The main reason is that the air is cleaner. For example, when my city closed its old town to traffic, children began to play in the streets again. So, in conclusion, the centre belongs to people, not to engines.

prompt.es: Escucha e indica qué parte de la intervención es una tangente.

choices.text: The claim that cities really do need more parks.
The story about her cousin's dog and a holiday.
The idea that people need somewhere quiet to relax.

feedback.es: La historia del perro y de las vacaciones se aparta del tema: ella misma lo admite con «sorry, I am rambling» antes de volver a su punto.

origin.audio: I believe cities need more parks. Well, my cousin lives near one, and she has a dog, and the dog, strangely, hates water, which reminds me of a holiday we took last year... sorry, I am rambling. Anyway, my point is that parks give people somewhere quiet to relax.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta está mejor ordenada y por qué?

choices.text: A, because it mentions more of her family and several friends.
Both, because each of them says something about trains and travel.
B, because it moves from point to reason, example and close.

feedback.es: La respuesta B sigue punto, razón, ejemplo y cierre; la A se dispersa en comentarios personales sin estructura.

origin.text: A: Well, I like trains, and my uncle used to drive one, but planes are faster, so perhaps, it depends. B: My point is that trains are better. The reason is that they are cleaner. For example, my commute is quiet. So, trains win.

prompt.es: Escucha las tres respuestas y elige la mejor ordenada.

choices.text: The second, because it is the only complete answer.
The first, because it mentions a member of the student's family.
The third, because it reaches its conclusion in far fewer words.
The second, because it is the longest of the three answers.

feedback.es: Solo la alumna que cita las notas de su primo reúne punto, razón, ejemplo y cierre en orden; ser la más larga no es el motivo.

origin.audio: The teacher asked three students whether school should start later. The first student said that he liked sleeping, that his brother never woke up on time and that mornings were, well, a bit grey, and then he trailed off. The second said that her point was yes; the main reason was that teenagers need more sleep; for example, her cousin's grades had improved after his school changed its hours; and in conclusion, later starts help everyone. The third said that her point was yes, that the main reason was that teenagers need sleep, and that, in conclusion, schools should start later.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué parte falta en la respuesta de la tercera alumna?

choices.text: A clear point.
A concrete example.
A supporting reason.
A closing sentence.

feedback.es: La tercera alumna da punto, razón y cierre, pero ningún caso concreto: le falta el ejemplo.

origin.audio: The teacher asked three students whether school should start later. The first student said that he liked sleeping, that his brother never woke up on time and that mornings were, well, a bit grey, and then he trailed off. The second said that her point was yes; the main reason was that teenagers need more sleep; for example, her cousin's grades had improved after his school changed its hours; and in conclusion, later starts help everyone. The third said that her point was yes, that the main reason was that teenagers need sleep, and that, in conclusion, schools should start later.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el profesor sobre la respuesta del alumno?

choices.text: That the order was sound, but the content made the argument hard to accept.
That the tangent was the best part, but it arrived too late in the answer.
That the content was sound, but its order made the argument hard to follow.
That the reason was weak, because it came straight after the example.

feedback.es: El profesor aprecia el punto y el ejemplo, pero dice que el oyente tuvo que trabajar para encontrar el argumento: el problema es el orden, no el contenido.

origin.text: Your answer had a clear point and a strong example, but the reason arrived only after a long tangent about your neighbour's garden. I am not saying the story was boring; I am saying that the listener had to work hard to find your argument, and in a minute of speaking, that effort is costly.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quiero desviarme del tema, así que vuelvo a mi razón principal.»

feedback.es: Go off on a tangent significa irse por las ramas; la expresión pide tangent.

origin.text: I do not want to go off on a ___, so let me return to my main reason and explain it with a clear example.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la entrenadora este comentario?

choices.text: To explain why a closing should introduce the speaker's strongest idea so far.
To point out that funding is too hard a topic for a short answer.
To suggest that two separate ideas make an answer more memorable.
To explain why a closing should return to the point instead of adding a topic.

feedback.es: La entrenadora señala que un cierre debe devolver al oyente a la idea principal; abrir otro tema deja dos ideas en lugar de una.

origin.text: You stated your point clearly and gave two good reasons, but then you ended with a brand-new idea about funding. A conclusion should not open a fresh topic. It should return to your point, so that the listener leaves with one idea in mind, not two separate ones.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Permíteme volver a la razón principal antes de cerrar.»

answer.text: Let me go back to my main reason before I close

feedback.es: Go back to my main reason es la fórmula para volver al hilo tras un desvío.

prompt.es: Une cada frase con lo que hace el hablante.

pairs: Sorry, I've drifted; let me get to the point.

pairs.es: Reconoces el desvío y vuelves al tema

pairs: In short, buses beat cars in this city.
To illustrate, my bus is never late.

feedback.es: Volver al tema con «get to the point», cerrar con «in short» e introducir un caso con «to illustrate» son tres funciones distintas.
